_comment: Tracks IETF/OpenID drafts implemented in this PoC. Updated daily by the standards-tracker GitHub Actions workflow. Set implemented_rev when the PoC code is updated to match a new revision.

wg_feeds.name: IETF WIMSE WG
wg_feeds.note: Discovers new WIMSE WG drafts not yet in our baseline

wg_feeds.name: IETF OAuth WG
wg_feeds.note: Discovers new OAuth WG drafts (DPoP updates, Transaction Tokens, etc.)

wg_feeds.name: OpenID Foundation
wg_feeds.note: Catches OIDF spec publications, errata, and public review periods

standards.label: WIMSE Workload Identity Credentials (WIT)
standards.impact: WIT claims structure (typ=wit+jwt), cnf.jwk format, SPIFFE URI sub

standards.label: WIMSE Workload Proof Token (WPT)
standards.impact: Breaking changes in -02: (1) WPT now conveyed via Authorization: WPT <token> instead of Workload-Proof-Token header; (2) ath claim removed; (3) error responses use 401 + WWW-Authenticate: WPT. Core claims unchanged: aud, wth, tth, jti.

standards.label: WIMSE Workload Identifier
standards.impact: SPIFFE URI format (spiffe://trust-domain/path), no query/fragment/port allowed

standards.label: WIMSE Mutual TLS Binding
standards.impact: X.509 URI SAN format, EC P-256 requirement, TLS 1.3 minimum

standards.label: WIMSE Architecture
standards.impact: Token exchange patterns at trust-domain boundaries, HTTP header names

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 Transaction Tokens (Txn-Token)
standards.impact: Txn-Token (txntoken+jwt) for call-chain context propagation; tth claim in WPT binds proof to transaction context; req_wl carries requesting workload SPIFFE ID

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 DPoP (RFC 9449)
standards.impact: DPoP proof JWT (dpop+jwt), cnf.jkt thumbprint binding

standards.label: OpenID Federation 1.0
standards.impact: Entity Configuration JWT, Subordinate Statement, authority_hints, trust chain resolution, min(EC.exp,SS.exp) caching

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 SPIFFE Client Authentication
standards.impact: WIT used as JWT bearer client assertion (client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer) to authenticate to OAuth AS — eliminates shared secrets for workload-to-OAuth-AS authentication

standards.label: OAuth Identity and Authorization Chaining Across Domains
standards.impact: JWT authorization grant (RFC 7523 profile) for cross-domain token exchange (RFC 8693); AS-A validates WIT and issues grant targeting AS-B; AS-B validates grant and issues its own access token; complements Txn-Token for multi-trust-domain chains

standards.label: JSON Web Token Best Current Practices
standards.impact: Compliance audit applied 2026-08-02: all validators now enforce WithValidMethods (ES256), WithExpirationRequired, WithIssuedAt, and typ header checks across pkg/wpt, pkg/sdwit, pkg/txntoken, pkg/identitychaining.

standards.label: WIMSE Workload-to-Workload Authentication with HTTP Signatures
standards.impact: Alternative to WPT (JWT-based) for workload-to-workload proof using RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures. pkg/httpsig implements Sign + Verify: Workload-Identity-Token header carries WIT, Signature-Input/Signature cover @method/@path/@query/workload-identity-token per §4. @authority excluded for TLS-proxy tolerance. ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 raw 64-byte r||s.

standards.label: WIMSE Workload Identity Practices
standards.impact: Directly aligned with this PoC: documents best practices for SPIFFE-based workload identity, short-lived WPT credential issuance, cert rotation, and no long-lived secrets. Validates the workload credential model in pkg/wit and pkg/wpt. Note: draft explicitly covers industry practices independent of WIMSE architecture specs — a useful cross-reference.
standards._triage: 2026-08-07: monitored. Best practices doc, not a protocol spec — primary home here in wimse-identity-fabric. Validates existing design choices. No implementation needed.

standards.label: AuthZEN Binding for OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
standards.impact: Externalises the AS policy decision in WPT Token Exchange to an AuthZEN PDP API. Relevant to pkg/tokenexchange: the 'which workload may exchange a WIT for a WPT targeting which audience' decision is exactly the policy seam this draft formalises. Rev 00 — monitor for when the WG adopts; implementation would add an AuthZEN client to the token exchange endpoint.
standards._triage: 2026-08-07: monitored. Rev 00, very early. High relevance to WPT token exchange and identity chaining policy decisions.

standards.label: AuthZEN Profile for OAuth 2.0 Token Issuance
standards.impact: Parent spec defining the AuthZEN five-tuple (subject, resource, action, context, environment) for externalising OAuth token issuance decisions to a PDP. Companion to AuthZEN-TE. Rev 00 — monitor.
standards._triage: 2026-08-07: monitored. Companion to authzen-token-exchange.

standards.label: Cross-Organizational Delegation for Workload and Agent Identity
standards.impact: Formalises cross-org delegation requirements — informs Phase 4 Token Exchange (internal/exchange) and Identity Chaining scenario.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: rev-02 read. Pure problem-statement + requirements doc — defines no new token types, claims, or wire formats. Confirms the multi-trust-domain delegation gap that identity chaining + token exchange address. No code change needed. Continue monitoring for when the WG issues a companion mechanism draft.

standards.label: SD-JWT-based Verifiable Digital Credentials (SD-JWT VC)
standards.impact: SD-JWT VC uses base SD-JWT for credential presentation (human-facing). Our pkg/sdwit uses base SD-JWT for M2M privacy (SD-WIT, typ=wit+sd-jwt) — intentionally NOT SD-JWT VC format. Distinction noted in Ch7 demo.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: at rev-19. Confirmed not-applicable: pkg/sdwit uses base SD-JWT for M2M workload privacy (SD-WIT, typ=wit+sd-jwt), not the SD-JWT VC credential presentation format. Distinction documented in Ch7 demo. No implementation needed.

standards.label: Identity Propagation Context for Multi-Hop Delegation in OAuth 2.0 Environments
standards.impact: Multi-hop identity propagation context — augments Ch8 Token Exchange and Identity Chaining scenarios. Tracked for future extension of pkg/identitychaining.

standards.label: Credential Delegation Protocol for AI Agents in Multi-System Environments
standards.impact: Formalises credential delegation semantics for AI agents across WIMSE trust domains — directly adjacent to the AgentChain and cross-domain delegation patterns. Monitor for WG adoption; if adopted would inform internal/exchange and identity-chaining cross-domain scenarios.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #4. Individual draft, relevant, no implementation change needed yet.

standards.label: OAuth Proof of Possession Tokens with HTTP Message Signatures
standards.impact: RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures as OAuth PoP mechanism — same design space as WPT per-request proof but using HTTP Signatures rather than a separate proof JWT. Complements draft-ietf-wimse-http-signature. Monitor: if WG adopts this direction it could affect the long-term role of WPT.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #4. Relevant to WPT design space, monitor only.

standards.label: JWT Profile for OAuth 2.0 Enveloped Proof of Possession (EPOP)
standards.impact: Enveloped PoP embeds proof inside the token rather than a separate JWT (DPoP/WPT pattern). Adjacent to WPT and DPoP; monitor for convergence with existing PoP mechanisms.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #4. Adjacent to WPT/DPoP design space, monitor only.

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 Delegated Authorization
standards.impact: OAuth delegated authorization patterns — could inform cross-domain token exchange (internal/exchange) and identity chaining scenarios. Monitor for M2M delegation relevance.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #4. Low-medium relevance, monitor only.

standards.label: Delegated Refresh Tokens for OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
standards.impact: Async delegated refresh tokens extending RFC 8693 token exchange. Tangentially relevant to cross-domain token exchange scenarios. Monitor only.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #4. Low relevance, monitor only.

standards.label: Cross-Device Flows: Security Best Current Practice
standards.impact: Human cross-device authentication flows (TV/IoT login). Not applicable — PoC focuses on M2M workload identity, not human-facing authentication.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #4. Dismissed — not relevant to M2M workload identity.

standards.label: CIBA Binding for OAuth Push-Based Authentication Device Discovery
standards.impact: Client Initiated Backchannel Authentication (CIBA) for human authentication via decoupled device. Not applicable — human-facing flow.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #4. Dismissed — not relevant to M2M workload identity.

standards.label: Discovery and Device Lifecycle for OAuth Push-Based Authentication
standards.impact: Device lifecycle for CIBA push-based human authentication. Not applicable — human-facing flow.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #4. Dismissed — not relevant to M2M workload identity.

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 Refresh Token Scope
standards.impact: Refresh token scope response for human OAuth clients. Not applicable — WIMSE workloads use short-lived token re-issuance, not refresh token flows.
standards._triage: 2026-08-04: assessed in issue #4. Dismissed — not relevant to M2M workload identity.

standards.label: Identity Continuation Assertion for OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
standards.impact: Defines an Identity Continuation Assertion (typ: oauth-identity-continuation+jwt, claims: identity_continuation_handle, act, cnf.jkt, jti, exp ≤300s) enabling intermediate workloads to obtain audience-specific user identity tokens without re-authentication, layered on RFC 8693 Token Exchange. Adjacent to pkg/identitychaining (jwt-authz-grant) and internal/exchange — but focuses on pairwise *user* subject propagation across IdP boundaries, not workload/SPIFFE identity. Monitor: if pattern gains WG traction it could complement or formalise cross-domain identity chaining.
standards._triage: 2026-08-05: assessed in issue #8. Addresses user (pairwise) subject propagation — different problem space from WIT workload identity. No implementation change needed; monitor for convergence with identity chaining.

standards.label: AAuth Protocol (Agentic Authorization)
standards.impact: OUT OF SCOPE for this workload identity PoC. AAuth is AI-agent-specific authorization — how agents request delegated permissions for sub-tasks. Primary coverage is in the wimse-agent-fabric PoC. No implementation planned here.

standards.label: Agent Authorization use cases and gap analysis
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: AI agent authz use cases — wimse-agent-fabric territory.

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 for Browser-Based Applications
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: Browser-based human authentication flows — not M2M workload identity.

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 RAR Metadata and Error Remediation
standards.impact: RAR (Rich Authorization Requests) metadata and error remediation. Tangentially relevant to structured authorization context in WPT/Txn-Token flows. Monitor.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: low direct relevance to workload identity. Monitor.

standards.label: OAuth Authorization Request Delegation Chain
standards.impact: Authorization request delegation chain — formalises delegation context in authorization requests. Adjacent to identity chaining and cross-org delegation scenarios.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: individual draft, early stage. Monitor for WG adoption.

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 Scope Aggregation for Multi-Step AI Agent Workflows
standards.impact: Multi-step AI agent scope aggregation across OAuth servers. Not applicable to this workload identity PoC — AI agent authorization scope is wimse-agent-fabric territory.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: AI agent authorization scope aggregation. Out of scope for wimse-identity-fabric.

standards.label: Updates to OAuth 2.0 JWT Client Authentication and Assertion-Based Authorization Grants
standards.impact: Tightens aud claim for client authentication JWTs: aud MUST be the AS issuer identifier URL, NOT the token endpoint URL. Introduces typ: "client-authentication+jwt". IMPORTANT: pkg/spiffeclientauth uses WIT (typ=wit+jwt) as client_assertion per draft-ietf-oauth-spiffe-client-auth — no direct impact now, but monitor: if spiffe-client-auth updates to require rfc7523bis aud constraints the WIT's aud value at the token endpoint would need to match the AS issuer ID.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: active-draft at rev-11. aud tightening for client-auth JWTs. No immediate code change — PoC uses WIT-as-assertion (its own typ), not the new client-authentication+jwt typ. Monitor for convergence with spiffe-client-auth draft.

standards.label: Token Status List (TSL)
standards.impact: Defines a status claim in WIT/WPT tokens pointing to a revocation bitmap endpoint. Currently PoC has no WIT revocation mechanism — short TTL is the primary defence. Monitor: if deployment scenarios require revocation before TTL expiry, TSL is the likely mechanism.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: WG document, active-draft. No immediate implementation — short-lived WIT model (5 min TTL) makes hard revocation optional. Track for future revocation scenarios.

standards.label: Condition-Bound Keys for Mutual-TLS Client Authentication and DPoP
standards.impact: Non-exfiltratable keys bound to presence/condition constraints — keys physically cannot leave the workload. Adjacent to pkg/keys/mtls.go and WPT cnf binding. Highly relevant if deployed in regulated or high-threat environments where key exfiltration is the primary risk.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: individual-draft, early stage. Relevant design direction for hardware-backed workload keys. Monitor for WG adoption.

standards.label: AuthZEN Profile for Authorization Claims in JWT Access Tokens
standards.impact: AuthZEN claims in JWT access tokens — companion to AuthZEN-TE and AuthZEN-Issuance. Monitor alongside those drafts.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: companion to authzen-token-exchange. Monitor.

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 Attestation Based Authorization for Native Applications
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: Attestation-based authz for native (human) apps — not applicable to M2M workload identity.

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 RAR Metadata and Error Remediation
standards.impact: Companion/update to draft-zehavi-oauth-rar-metadata for RAR error remediation. Tangentially relevant. Monitor.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: RAR remediation companion. Low direct relevance. Monitor.

standards.label: Verifiable Attenuated Delegation for AI Agent Chains
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: Verifiable attenuated delegation for AI agent chains — wimse-agent-fabric territory.

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 for First-Party Applications
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: First-party human OAuth flows — not M2M workload identity.

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 Policy-Based Anonymous Access Tokens
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: Privacy-preserving anonymous access tokens for human subjects — not applicable.

standards.label: OAuth Profile for Delegated AI Agent Authorization
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: AI agent OAuth delegation grants — wimse-agent-fabric territory.

standards.label: An Attenuated Delegation Profile for Automated Agents
standards.impact: Attenuated delegation profile for AI agents — capability-restricted delegation tokens for sub-agents. Out of scope here; primary coverage in wimse-agent-fabric PoC.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: AI agent delegation, attenuated authority. wimse-agent-fabric territory.

standards.label: OAuth Subject Signing Key Binding for Resource Servers
standards.impact: Defines subject_keys JWK Set claim in JWT access tokens — distinct from cnf (sender-constraining). Enables RS to verify authorization evidence signed by the subject, not just sender-constrained PoP. Adjacent to WPT cnf binding but different use case. Low immediate relevance; monitor.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: individual-draft -00. subject_keys vs cnf distinction is important but no implementation needed — WPT cnf binding is sender-constraining, not subject-signing. Monitor.

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 Attestation-Based Client Authentication
standards.impact: WG document defining attestation-based client authentication (client-attestation+jwt). Directly adjacent to pkg/spiffeclientauth — workload attestation evidence could replace or augment WIT-based client auth. Monitor closely.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: active-draft WG document. Close design space to spiffe-client-auth and rfc7523bis. Track for potential future replacement of WIT-as-assertion pattern.

standards.label: The OAuth 2.1 Authorization Framework
standards.impact: OAuth 2.1 consolidation — removes implicit flow, mandates PKCE, tightens redirect URI validation. Underpins all OAuth-based specs here. Monitor: if AS implementations update to OAuth 2.1-only, check token exchange and client credentials flows.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: base spec update. No immediate code change — PoC uses client_credentials + token exchange, both retained in 2.1. Monitor for breaking changes.

standards.label: X.509 Certificate Bearer Profile for OAuth 2.0 Client Authentication and Authorization Grants
standards.impact: X.509 certificate bearer profile for OAuth client auth — adjacent to mTLS binding in pkg/keys/mtls.go. Monitor for convergence with WIMSE mTLS spec.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: X.509 bearer adjacent to mTLS. Monitor.

standards.label: Aggregate Signatures for WIMSE Delegation-Chain Integrity
standards.impact: Profiles WIMSE HTTP Message Signatures for request chains: introduces Signature-Aggregate header, wimse-req-digest and wimse-resp-digest parameters. Prevents undetectable signature removal from delegation chains; size stays constant (vs. linear growth). BLS signatures as primary instantiation. Directly relevant to pkg/identitychaining and internal/exchange if HTTP-based delegation chain integrity is needed.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: WIMSE WG individual draft at -00. Very early but directly relevant to delegation chain integrity. Monitor for WG adoption and convergence with draft-ietf-wimse-http-signature.

standards.label: AI Agent Authentication and Authorization
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: AI Agent Authentication and Authorization — wimse-agent-fabric territory.

standards.label: Transaction Token Authorization Grant Profile for OAuth Identity and Authorization Chaining
standards.impact: Transaction Token Authorization Grant Profile for OAuth identity and authorization chaining. Directly relevant to pkg/txntoken and internal/exchange — formalises how Txn-Tokens chain across OAuth AS boundaries. Monitor for convergence with draft-ietf-oauth-transaction-tokens.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: individual draft -00. Adjacent to transaction tokens and identity chaining. Monitor.

standards.label: Authorization Posture Mechanism (APM): Per-Transaction Consistency for OAuth 2.0
standards.impact: Authorization Posture Mechanism — per-transaction consistency check for OAuth flows. Could complement token exchange in multi-hop scenarios. Monitor.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: individual draft at -00. Novel per-transaction posture concept. Monitor.

standards.label: Revocation Closure for Agentic Authorization Systems
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: Revocation closure for agentic authorization — wimse-agent-fabric territory.

standards.label: AI Identity Management System
standards.impact: WIMSE WG newly adopted draft on AI Identity Management System. Extends WIMSE workload identity model to AI agent deployments — high relevance to agent fabric but also informs how identity fabric handles AI workloads. Monitor closely as it matures.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: newly adopted WIMSE WG document at -00. AI identity management — relevant to both fabric PoCs. Monitor.

standards.label: Deferred Token Response
standards.impact: Deferred token response for async token issuance — relevant if token exchange needs async policy evaluation (e.g., AuthZEN PDP with latency). Monitor.
standards._triage: 2026-09-18: async token response pattern. Low immediate relevance — synchronous exchange today. Monitor.
